blindSummary:
This state/province, the country's capital jurisdiction, concentrates enforcement activity of the national anti-LGBT framework: club raids, the arrest of the first person charged with creating an extremist organisation on LGBT grounds (late December 2024), and the medical and bureaucratic gatekeeping that the 2023 national transition ban imposes. A 2025 survey of persecution by an exiled independent news outlet is titled around "arrests, club raids and extremism charges." A foreign visitor encountering the local police faces the national propaganda-law penalty — up to 15 days' detention and deportation — applied in the jurisdiction with the highest police density and most active venue-level enforcement in the country.

Local risk sits slightly below the country-wide average. The severity of the law is identical everywhere (it is national), but this state/province's role as the primary venue for enforcement operations and its concentration of bureaucratic touchpoints (document verification, medical access, hotel registration) materially raise a visitor's probability of encountering active application. It is comparable to one other regional jurisdiction, which produced the country's first criminal extremism conviction against a commercial venue; both represent enforcement-active jurisdictions within the uniform national framework.
